tasks.short: Explain design specifications to test engineers

steps.what: Ask which specification version to test
Open the signed specification version
Draft an explanation that cites clauses

loop.input: clause ids and the engineer's questions
loop.output: note that cites clause ids only
loop.check: Every clause id in the note exists on that specification version
loop.stop: One draft; leave a blank where a question has no clause
loop.why_not_simpler: A clause written for one site does not match the next by a lookup

steps.what: Explain the specification in the room
Sign this explanation note version
List questions the note did not answer

tasks.design: The network engineer asks which specification version to test. The architect opens that version in {DOCS} and a bounded note cites only its clause ids. The architect explains it in the room and signs the note. The engineer tests against the signed note, not against the meeting alone.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explanations were spoken, and the specification moved, so a later test could not tell which clauses had been covered.
tasks.enabler_now: Clause ids on a named specification version can be checked against the note.
tasks.still_hard: The questions that are not in the text still need the architect in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The architect decides which clauses matter for this test and signs the note.

ambition.what: Explain a specification again when its version changes, not only at the first meeting

tasks.altitude: Less time reconstructing what was said. The architect can refuse a test that uses an unsigned explanation. The room stays.

reach.task: Test only the clauses named in the signed note
reach.learn: Which specification version was explained and which questions were left open

evidence.claim: Explaining a specification is a meeting plus a document. The document can cite clauses. The meeting cannot be skipped.
Digest [S3] says a document product can fill metadata from a prompt, and the vendor warns the fill can be wrong, so clause ids are checked against the specification rather than filled in.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. Integration and test engineers are the network engineer in this firm. The task ends when the signed explanation note is the version the engineer will test.

Input contract: specification version, clause id, question, site. Producer of the question is the network engineer. Producer of the clauses is the signed specification. A question with no clause id stays on an open list.
The automate class fits the written note, not the explanation in the room. That room time is not treated as saved. Use the document store's own versions before custom code.
unknowns: Whether more than one specification version is live for the same site.
Who explains the specification when the architect is absent.
research_questions: How often does a test use a specification version older than the signed note?
What share of engineer questions has no matching clause?

already_counted.description: Architect still explains the hard clauses in the room
Architect edits the note before signing

incremental.description: Update the note template when a new specification section appears
Engineers resend a question that names no version

approvals.approved_version: explanation note signed for this specification version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes specifications are still unmarked prose, so the note cites little and the explanation in the room is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set procedures that report network availability

steps.what: Read network availability counters
Choose which counters the procedure keeps
Draft the procedure from those counters

loop.input: chosen counter ids and the procedure template
loop.output: text that names only those counters
loop.check: Every counter name in the text is one of the chosen ids
loop.stop: Stop the section if a sentence names a counter that was not chosen
loop.why_not_simpler: Threshold words differ by link and a fixed template cannot write them

steps.what: Sign the availability procedure version
Refresh the monthly utilization extract
Read the extract for the service

tasks.design: Link and site counters already sit in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The architect chooses which counters a procedure keeps and signs that list in {DOCS}. A {BI} extract then refreshes availability, capacity and utilization from those ids only. Totals stay on the link and the site, not on a person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each monthly pack was rebuilt in a sheet, and the counters in it changed without a named procedure.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring already stores a counter id, a link id and a time, so an extract can repeat.
tasks.still_hard: Which counters matter, and what threshold the business will accept, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The architect chooses the counters and the threshold, and signs the procedure.

ambition.what: Review a link when it crosses the signed threshold, not only in the yearly plan

tasks.altitude: The monthly extract stops being recopied. The architect can refuse a figure that is not in the signed procedure.

reach.task: Read the monthly extract against the signed procedure
reach.learn: Which counters are in the procedure and which links crossed the threshold

evidence.claim: Network monitors in a mid-size firm already count availability and utilization. The remaining work is which counters to keep and what the threshold means.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. This extract keeps link and site totals, not a person's traffic.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. A view by person is out of this procedure.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and, for firms in scope, includes continuity measures. Sector and size decide scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task is the procedure and the monthly extract, not a live capacity change.
Input contract: counter id, link id, site, period, value. Producer is the monitoring export. A counter with no link id is left off the procedure.

The prior that standard software does not fit is wrong for the counters: monitoring already stores them. Configure that export before custom code. A per-person usage view is not built, so works-council consent for staff monitoring is not triggered. Whether the firm is in scope of the cyber duty of care is a separate fact.
unknowns: Whether this firm is in scope of the Dutch cyber duty of care.
Which links have no counter id.
Who signs the procedure when the architect is absent.
research_questions: What share of links has no counter for a full month?
How often does the signed counter list change?

already_counted.description: Architect's choice of counters and thresholds
Architect edits procedure sentences before signing

incremental.description: Add a counter id when a new link type is monitored
Service owners query a link the extract left blank

approvals.approved_version: availability procedure signed for this period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many links have no counter id, so the extract is partial and every procedure choice still takes a full review. Per-person traffic is not part of the saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate designs with linked network designers

steps.what: Send constraints for the linked network
Log each open interface point
Draft the interface sheet from points

loop.output: sheet that cites point ids only
loop.check: Every constraint cites a logged point id
loop.stop: One pass; drop a constraint with no point id
loop.why_not_simpler: The other network's limits are free text, not a fixed form

steps.what: Agree the interface with the vendor
File the agreed interface version
Adjust the internal design to match

tasks.design: The vendor engineer sends interface constraints for the linked network. Open points are logged on a {WORKFLOW} form with an owner. A bounded sheet in {DOCS} cites only those points. The architect agrees the interface in a meeting and files that version. Applying it on the live link is a later change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Constraints arrived as long mail threads, so two designers could be working from different limits.
tasks.enabler_now: A point id, an owner and a design version can be stored on one line.
tasks.still_hard: What the other network will actually accept is settled in the meeting, not by the sheet.
tasks.human_edge: The architect agrees or refuses an interface and signs the version.

ambition.what: Re-agree the interface when either design version changes, not only at project start

tasks.altitude: Less time reconstructing the thread. The architect can refuse a build that uses an unsigned interface. The meeting stays.

reach.task: Build the linked network to the agreed interface version
reach.learn: Which points were agreed and which were left open

evidence.claim: Coordinating a linked network is a meeting with another designer. The thread can be logged. The agreement cannot be skipped.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so the agreed interface is filed for a person to apply later, not applied unattended.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The associated designer is the vendor engineer. The task ends when the interface version is filed. Changing the live link is out of this task.

Input contract: point id, link name, constraint, owner, their design version, our design version. Producer is the vendor engineer. A constraint with no point id is raised in the meeting and not written into the sheet.
Use the form's own list before custom code. The meeting prior fits the agreement and is not treated as saved.
unknowns: Whether the linked network is a supplier, a partner, or another internal domain.
Who may agree an interface when the architect is absent.
research_questions: What share of interface points is still only in mail?
How often does a filed interface change before build?

already_counted.description: Architect's time agreeing the interface in the meeting
Architect edits the sheet before the meeting

incremental.description: Extend the point form when a new constraint type appears
Vendor engineer resends a constraint that has no owner

approvals.approved_version: interface agreement signed in this meeting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes interface constraints arrive as long mail, so the sheet is thin and the meeting with the vendor engineer is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and monitor project schedules and budgets

steps.what: Enter dates, amounts and task ids
Flag tasks past date or amount
Draft a note from the flagged tasks

loop.output: note that cites task ids over the line
loop.check: Every cited task id is on the flagged list
loop.stop: One draft; do not explain a row that is not flagged
loop.why_not_simpler: The reason a date slipped is not stored as a code

steps.what: Decide which project variance to accept
File the signed schedule version
Confirm the filed project schedule

tasks.design: The project controller enters task id, date, cost centre and amount in {PROJECT}. A {BI} view flags lines past the date or over the amount. A bounded note cites only flagged task ids. The architect accepts or refuses the variance and the signed schedule version is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates and amounts were copied into a fresh pack each month, so a flag could not tell a real overrun from a stale cell.
tasks.enabler_now: Task id, planned date and amount can be compared with the current date and the spent amount.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a slipped date is acceptable is still the architect's call.
tasks.human_edge: The architect accepts or refuses a variance and signs the schedule version.

ambition.what: Accept or refuse a variance in the week it appears, not at month end

tasks.altitude: The flag list replaces the recopied pack. The architect can ignore a line that is not actually over, and still decides the ones that are.

reach.task: Update the budget from the signed schedule version
reach.learn: Which variances were accepted and which were refused

evidence.claim: Schedule and cost control in a mid-size firm is a dated list plus a decision on the lines that slipped. The list can be compared. The decision cannot.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. Hours here stay on the task id, not on a named employee.

assumptions: Focal role is the network architect. The task ends at a signed schedule version. It does not move money.
Input contract: task id, planned date, actual date, cost centre, planned amount, spent amount. Producer is the project controller. A row with no task id is not flagged.

Use the project tool's own date and amount fields before custom code. The meeting prior fits the variance decision, not the flagging. Cost is not broken out by person, so this is not staff monitoring.
unknowns: Which tasks have no planned date.
Who may accept a variance above a given amount.
research_questions: What share of tasks has a date but no amount?
How often is the first flag a stale row?

already_counted.description: Architect edits the variance note before the decision

incremental.description: Adjust the flag rules when a new cost centre is added
Project controller corrects rows that have no task id

approvals.approved_version: schedule decision signed for these flagged task ids

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes dates and amounts stay incomplete, so the flag list is short and the variance decision is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The architect still explains a specification and agrees an interface in person, and stops retyping availability sheets, agendas and schedule lines.
reach: Network engineers test against a signed explanation, not a remembered meeting.
Service owners read a monthly extract tied to a procedure version.
Vendor engineers work from an agreed interface version.
Project controllers see a variance in the week it crosses the signed line.
skills_to_grow: Explain a specification as clauses a note can cite.
Choose availability counters before a report is drawn.
Write an interface agreement as a version, not a thread.
Accept a schedule variance against a dated amount.
role.ambitious_version: A specification change, a link threshold and a cost overrun each get a decision in the week they appear.
